title: Cross-Section Avatar
content:
Related to this previous Community (Archive) post: <https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/community/posts/900002139306-How-to-see-sectional-view>

I would like to be able to take a cross-sectional 'slice' of an avatar. For example, the armhole or crotch/hip cross-section would be useful when drafting a sleeve or trouser, respectively.

The finished 'shape' of a section cannot be determined from 2D flat-pattern drafting, but has direct carryover to it when drafting from scratch.

  
  
Is this something that can be done in CLO3D?  
  
If not, are there any suggested alternatives?  
  
@r901207 which software did you end up using?  
  
Thank you!


### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: This is possible for the different components of the avatar, but the options are limited. Right-click on a part of the avatar and choose deactivate/hide from the menu.

Comment 2: You could in another 3D package like blender or zbrush boolean off an arm or cross section. Possibly even in a 3D slicer package also.
content_description: This web page aims to explore the possibility of creating cross-sectional slices of avatars in CLO3D for enhanced garment drafting, while also seeking alternative solutions and user experiences.

title: CLO Python API
content:
what is difference between ExpertOBJ and ExpertOBJW


### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: "The "w" in the string stands for the word "wide" indicating that it handles wide character encodings, which usually require more than one byte per character. This makes wstring suitable for supporting a large character set, including Unicode characters and characters from various languages." So for file names with the e.g. Latin alphabet, it suffices to use exportOBJ, but if for example Chinese or Japanese characters are used, it is best to use exportOBJW.

Comment 2: We have inquired about this and will get back to you asap.

title: Silicone/Rubber dipped drawstring
content:
Does anyone have any tips on how to create this silicone rubber texture in CLO?   
I have already made the drastring, just need help with the texture! :)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/fe8425513b88465f804aa7dd8df14ba9/images/2f21ef308f6e42c8b2167dfb6c1e7633Hoodie-Cord-with-Coated-Silicone.png)


### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Thank you for your comments! I will do my best :)

Comment 2: I did a close study but unfortunately I can't post a photo from here. You shouldn't think like a pattern, you should think like a 3D solid object in CLO. It will consist of 4 piecesStepsFabric: Plastic1. Draw a circle for the bottom pieceWidth: 1.7 cmHight1.7 cmTchickness 50 mmParticle distance 1 mmCurvature %20Resolution 102. Draw a circle for the top pieceWidth: 1.5 cmHight 1.5 cmTchickness 50 mmParticle distance 1 mmCurvature %20Resolution 103. Draw a circle for the middle large pieceWidth: 2.5 cmHight 2.5 cmTchickness 30 mmParticle distance 1 mmCurvature %100Resolution 104. Draw a circle for the middle small pieceWidth: 1.8 cmHight 1.8 cmTchickness 30 mmParticle distance 1 mmCurvature 100%Resolution 10Add UV PackagingExport obj (thick)Import obj (Select Trim)Material PlasticSave Trim
Reply 1: Hello, I'm Robin, the Product Manager at CONNECT.We'll work on improving the platform so you can post images in comments for a better communication experience.

Comment 3: Cut the end part you want to make silicone and separate the cord. Delete the cord. There should be no texture in the remaining part. Export as obj. Then add it to your file as trim and choose plastic as material. If not, I think you can try to make your obj file look like this in blender.

Comment 4: Hi, I've tried two options, both of which were unsatisfactory. Using a displacement map doesn't create this look (the knot is still "comparted" and not "coated") and trying to wrap a pattern piece around the knotted part and shrink that in so that it causes the "coated" effect also didn't work. So if anyone else has an idea?
Reply 1: I did a close study but unfortunately I can't post a photo from here. You shouldn't think like a pattern, you should think like a 3D solid object in CLO. It will consist of 4 piecesStepsFabric: Plastic1. Draw a circle for the bottom pieceWidth: 1.7 cmHight1.7 cmTchickness 50 mmParticle distance 1 mmCurvature %20Resolution 102. Draw a circle for the top pieceWidth: 1.5 cmHight 1.5 cmTchickness 50 mmParticle distance 1 mmCurvature %20Resolution 103. Draw a circle for the middle large pieceWidth: 2.5 cmHight 2.5 cmTchickness 30 mmParticle distance 1 mmCurvature %100Resolution 104. Draw a circle for the middle small pieceWidth: 1.8 cmHight 1.8 cmTchickness 30 mmParticle distance 1 mmCurvature 100%Resolution 10Add UV PackagingExport obj (thick)Import obj (Select Trim)Material PlasticSave Trim

title: Truing a Graded Pattern
content:
Been loving all the great features, however I find the grading features of 2D patterns incomplete. I have a graded style, but I need to fine tune and true the sleeve cap into the armhole. Ideally I can see line length for each graded size in the "Edit grading curve (Each)" function. But I can only see line length of the base size which is uneditable. It is feeling clumsy. I would love some help. Thank You

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/e5b2064378f242028034b8923dc31f76/images/5d6e036413814ad9a4c10db3bb4eb9ffScreenshot%202025-01-04%20at%201.19.25%E2%80%AFPM.png)


### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi Benjamin. Thank you for your feedback. Currently this would be a Feature Request which we will forward onto our team.A current work around would be to Trace the Line as a Point of Measure (POM). You would then be able to see each line length in the POM tab
content_description: "Enhance your grading experience by providing feedback on the need for improved functionalities in the 2D patterns grading feature, specifically for fine-tuning sleeve caps into armholes."
